rootCause.mechanism: the machine entered Clamshell Sleep 92 seconds into the validation run. macOS suspends process execution across sleep while the wall clock keeps advancing, so a vitest testTimeout measured in wall-clock time expires without the test body having been given any CPU.
rootCause.caffeinateDoesNotPreventClamshellSleep: the run was launched under caffeinate -dimsu. That assertion prevents IDLE system sleep; it does not prevent the sleep caused by closing the lid. Closing the lid on battery sleeps the machine regardless, which is why a pre-start lid check - which samples one instant - cannot by itself protect a multi-minute run.

clamshellSleep.durationCorroborated: 17:59:10 + 993 s = 18:15:43 local, exactly the next DarkWake, so the trailing 'N secs' is the true suspension length

mechanicalProof.1_sleepOccurredDuringValidation: the Clamshell Sleep at 15:59:10Z lies strictly between VALIDATE_START 15:57:38Z and VALIDATE_EXIT 16:18:44Z
mechanicalProof.2_executionWasSuspended: a 993-second suspension inside a 1266-second run; the gate's own post-run probe recorded the last Sleep/Wake event moving from '2026-09-24 17:35:54' to '2026-09-24 18:18:43', i.e. unchanged=no

3_timeoutIsIncompatibleWithAnUninterrupt.statement: 1,005,926 ms of wall clock against a 30,000 ms budget is only reachable if the process was not running. Subtracting the 993,000 ms suspension leaves 12,926 ms of awake time, comfortably inside the budget.

4_zeroAssertionFailures.method: the Failed Tests block of the preserved log contains no AssertionError, no 'expected ... to be/equal' and no toBe(/toEqual( occurrence; the sole failure line is 'Error: Test timed out in 30000ms.'

5_runLevelCorroboration.statement: sleep-adjusted, the whole run took 250.57 awake seconds, squarely inside this host's measured healthy band. The host was not slow and the suite was not failing; suspension was inserted into its clock.
